meta.title: InterContinental Danang Resort: Honest Review After 4 Nights (Worth It?)
meta.description:
Is the InterContinental Danang Sun Peninsula actually a world-class 5-star resort? After our 4-night stay at this 100-acre luxury hotel, we are sharing everything: the good, the bad, and the things the review sites don't tell you. We stayed in the Club Terrace Suite Panoramic Ocean View and explored every corner of this stunning cliffside resort. From the breakfast buffet and Michelin-starred restaurant to the Olympic-sized infinity pool, the private beach, and the funicular tram, we covered it all.

🏨 Check out our Capella Hanoi Hotel review, as it is also designed by Bill Bensley, who designed InterContinental Danang: https://youtu.be/fFqCh6ivivE

comments.author: @Houstonclarke
comments.text: This hotel was so exotic and magical. I didn’t believe we would see so many monkeys, and they were so surreal—so beautiful it was hard to believe they were real! If the heat hadn’t been so oppressive this would have been a near perfect stay.

comments.author: @JoonBug777
comments.text: Agreed. Perhaps, some people won't mind the heat as much. If so, this would be merely a perfect stay for them. ^^ Omg, it was so hot and humid. 😅😅

comments.author: @main2333
comments.text: Go on cooler months. Thank goodness im used to heat living in hawaii and born in vietnam. If its humid may be high up in the mountains. Cant wait to stay thier when i move to retire. Bucket list!

comments.author: @Coconutcrabs
comments.text: Very informative video, thanks for sharing. Quick question, did you have to tip the buggy driver each time and how much? Also what about the lady that show you the room in the beginning, did you have to tip her as well? I'm heading there in two weeks, so just curious how the tipping works. Thanks for your reply.

comments.author: @JoonBug777
comments.text: Thanks for watching! Great questions! We didn't tip any of those folks, including buggy drivers, the staff who introduced the room, and any other guest services. We tipped at restaurants and bars  if we felt the service and food were great. But, not a lot. Just a few US dollars, not based on percentage. We also left a couple of bucks tip for housekeeping after the first night so they are motivated to do a great job. I wouldn't worry about it. They didn't give pressure or acted awkward in anyway without tips.

comments.author: @JoonBug777
comments.text: Thanks so much for watching and leaving a comment. ^^

comments.author: @main2333
comments.text: After working so hard in US. This will be my first place to stay for a pver due RRR. I want to invite my family that lives in Vietnam to stay with me too. Do they have family rooms?

comments.author: @JoonBug777
comments.text: How lovely you are to invite your family! Yes, they do have bigger suites with multiple rooms and beds you can choose from! You will be able to look into them on their website.
